transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Tina (Redwood SE), Lena (Cinderfall CTO), Diego (Head of ML), Rita (VP Eng), Samir (Infra), Olivia (PM)
---
Summary: quick discovery for Cinderfall's roadmap to integrate a text-generation API for product recommendations and support triage. Customer evaluating PLG/self-serve Redwood API first (fast time-to-first-token), then potential Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) for PII-sensitive workloads. Important constraints: data residency for EU customers, HSM/KMS integration, latency SLO ~150ms p95 for short prompts, and predictable unit cost for high QPS.
Topics: free credits & time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private fit, security/compliance (SOC2/KMS/HSM), batching and cost controls, rollout strategy and canary, benchmarks and perf criteria.
Action items (captured verbally): see metadata list above.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intro, i'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, with Jonas and Tina from our solutions team, how's everybody do- doing?
[00:07] Lena: good thanks, lena here, uh we were excited to chat — we've been looking at a few providers, wanted to see the quickstart path.
[00:12] Diego: hey, diego — quick note, primary goal is to get a prototype live in a sprint, understand token economics and, um, how we move to private infra for PII.
[00:22] Jonas: perfect, that aligns, we'll walk through time-to-first-token, the free credits flow, and typical migration from hosted to Dedicated or Private. we'll also call out perf benchmark approach.
[00:31] Rita: clarity up front — latency SLO, around 150ms p95 for short completions, otherwise, this becomes tricky for product UX. we also must keep EU data in EU zones.
[00:41] Maya: understood, noted. Samir, are there specific network constraints?
[00:44] Samir: yeah, we have strict egress controls and our KMS is in Azure Key Vault; if we do Private deployed in our VNet we need HSM integration or bring-your-own-KMS.
[00:55] Tina: got it — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and can integrate with HSMs via our Private controllers, and for Dedicated we offer VPC peering and customer KMS options as well. sometimes there's a term mix, we can surface the ops doc.
[01:07] Olivia: how fast can we do the first call? one engineer should get a result in the day ideally.
[01:11] Jonas: with our PLG flow, you can sign up, we'll drop 30k credits into your org, and a dev can hit the hosted API within an hour. we've seen teams reach a meaningful prototype in a few hours to a day.
[01:21] Diego: what do you mean by credits — is it tokens? how transparent is cost per token?
[01:25] Maya: credits map to token units in the console, but we'll share a token-cost spreadsheet. hosted pricing is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is reserved capacity that gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at commit. Private is licensed for air-gapped/regulatory.
[01:36] Lena: okay. for sensitive requests we want inference to happen inside our VPC; other non-sensitive can go to hosted. is hybrid routing possible?
[01:44] Jonas: yes, you can configure routing policies — route by data classification, latency target, or cost tier. automatic fallback to a compatible hosted variant if Dedicated capacity is saturated is supported.
[01:56] Rita: you mentioned model variants — are those quantized models? how does quality compare?
[02:02] Tina: we curate model variants and quantization profiles per workload. smaller quantized variants reduce cost and memory but can affect quality on nuanced prompts. Redwood Optimize recommends profiles based on evaluation sets.
[02:16] Diego: that sounds good; we need to run a couple of evals against our prompt set to measure regression risk.
[02:21] Jonas: we can run a batch eval during the pilot; we usually surface a quality delta chart per metric.
[02:27] [short crosstalk]
[02:30] Maya: quick question for process — Rita, what's the expected procurement timeline if the pilot looks good?
[02:35] Rita: ideally 6–8 weeks for Dedicated procurement, maybe faster if legal's not heavy; for PLG, we can be live without procurement for a dev prototype.
[02:45] Samir: two more infra notes: 1) we need audit logs and token-level traceability for compliance, and 2) we want a plan to rotate KMS keys without downtime.
[02:54] Tina: both supported — audit logs streaming to your SIEM via an agent or S3, and key rotation steps are in our ops runbook; we'll send the runbook link.
[03:05] Lena: what's the typical throughput for a single Dedicated pool? we may have spikes up to 300 rps for simple embedding calls during batch processing windows.
[03:15] Jonas: Dedicated pools are configurable — we size by GPU type and batch configs; for 300 rps low-latency token generation you might want a mixture of smaller instances to get warm KV cache hit ratio. we'll propose a sizing estimate after seeing token length distribution.
[03:30] Diego: speaking of KV cache — how do you handle cold-start costs? we've seen huge token costs when context windows reload.
[03:37] Jonas: we do prefix caching and keep warm caches for hot routes; batching policies and dynamic KV replication reduce cold-starts. but if bursts are unpredictable, autoscale plus reserved burst capacity helps mitigate cost spikes.
[03:50] Maya: for the PLG pilot, most customers start with hosted, quick eval, then a Dedicated commit if predictable load. Private is common for regulated workflows where data cannot leave the VNet.
[04:02] Rita: how does observability look? can product teams see token-level cost per route?
[04:07] Tina: yes, Redwood Console has per-route breakdowns, token cost, latency heatmaps, and tracing hooks. you can restrict access with RBAC and SSO.
[04:15] Lena: security — can we get SOC2 and penetration test reports?
[04:18] Maya: yes, we'll send SOC2 and recent pentest summary in the security pack. also include our network architecture for Private and Dedicated.
[04:26] Samir: what's the expected size of the integration work to test a single endpoint? we need a dev ticket estimate.
[04:31] Jonas: for a basic proxy integration to our API it's minimal — one engineer can wire up auth and call flows in a day. for on-prem Private, the setup is heavier — we estimate 2–3 weeks for packaging and validation depending on firewall rules.
[04:47] Diego: if we use hosted for the early phase, how do we guarantee EU data residency?
[04:51] Maya: hosted endpoints let you choose region; we have EU regions and can pin requests to those regions. for stricter guarantees, Private/VPC is recommended.
[04:59] Olivia: for the prototype, the PM question: is streaming available from hosted? low-latency streaming matters for UI.
[05:04] Tina: yes streaming is available; we support chunked responses and function-style tool calls. streaming latency is subject to the same p95 SLOs but typical token relay is <50ms per token in our EU/NA regions for small models.
[05:18] Rita: cost control — we need throttles and quota enforcement per route.
[05:22] Jonas: quotas, rate limiting, and token caps are configurable per API key. you can set per-team quotas in the console.
[05:30] Lena: any gotchas around redaction or data retention if we log requests for metrics?
[05:35] Tina: you control retention; for privacy you can disable request body logging. we offer selective redaction and PII filters. in Dedicated/Private you can choose not to persist logs off-host.
[05:47] [silence / note taking]
[06:00] Maya: ok, let's sketch next steps — we'll provision PLG credits and a sandbox org for you to try the hosted API, send the security pack, and set up a benchmarking deep-dive with Diego + Jonas.
[06:12] Diego: i'd like a bench that mirrors our prompt lengths and concurrency; can you run the same prompt set?
[06:18] Jonas: yes, send the prompt set and sample keys, we'll run a perf script and return the result with suggestions for batching and quantization.
[06:26] Rita: we'll need a pricing estimate for a 3-month Dedicated commit if the pilot looks good.
[06:31] Maya: we'll share a Dedicated pricing matrix and a sample SLO addendum.
[06:35] Samir: one more question about fallback: if Dedicated is down or overloaded, you said there can be automatic fallback to hosted. is that configured per route?
[06:42] Tina: yes, per-route fallback policy — you can opt into graceful degradation or strict failover. we also support A/B rollout rules for model variants.
[06:52] Lena: curious — who else are you seeing in this space that does Private well? are there big gaps versus self-hosted open-source runtimes?
[06:59] Jonas: some customers compare us to self-managed runtimes or vendors that focus on single-node inference. our differentiation is the orchestration layer — unified API across hosted/dedicated/private plus built-in observability and automated routing. competitors like Anthropic/OpenAI are more model-first; replicate is more self-hosted marketplace.
[07:20] Diego: any clients in regulated healthcare that did hybrid?
[07:23] Maya: yes, a couple of healthtechs ran patient-facing low-risk flows on hosted and shifted PHI to a Private VPC for high-risk. we can share anonymized case studies.
[07:33] [brief pause]
[07:40] Olivia: timeline — can we do the prototype this week?
[07:43] Maya: we'll provision the credits today and email the sign-up link; development can start within hours.
[07:49] Jonas: propose we schedule the benchmark session on Wednesday or Thursday next week — Diego and Samir, what fits?
[07:57] Samir: Wednesday morning works.
[08:00] Diego: Wednesday is good.
[08:03] Maya: great. recap and parking lot: Maya to send security pack and PLG credits, Jonas to prepare benchmark script, Rita to confirm procurement timeline and pilot success criteria.
[08:14] Lena: success criteria for us: 1) prototype with integrated calls, 2) latency p95 under 150ms for core routes, 3) clear cost per token estimate and Dedicated sizing, 4) data residency path.
[08:28] Maya: good criteria. we'll include them in the follow-up email.
[08:33] [several attendees nodding]
[08:40] Maya: any other Qs?
[08:42] Rita: none from me.
[08:44] Diego: no.
[08:45] Lena: no, thanks.
[08:46] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.
---
